lessons.title: Counting: один agrees, два to четыре take the genitive singular, five and up take the genitive plural
lessons.explanation:
Russian counting is a case system rather than a list of number words, and the case is chosen by the last numeral you say. The rule has three bands. один (a-DEEN, 'one') is a special adjective and agrees with its noun in gender, number and case, so it has four nominative shapes: один стол (a-DEEN STOL, 'one table'), одна книга (ad-NA KNEE-ga, 'one book'), одно окно (ad-NO ak-NO, 'one window'), and одни часы (ad-NEE cha-SY, 'one watch'), where the plural is forced because часы has no singular. два, три and четыре take the genitive singular, and два has a gender split: два стола (DVA sta-LA, 'two tables') but две книги (dvye KNEE-gee, 'two books'), три окна (tree ak-NA, 'three windows'), четыре стола. Five and above take the genitive plural: пять столов (PYAT sta-LOF, 'five tables'), шесть книг (shest kneek, 'six books'), десять окон (DYE-seet O-kan, 'ten windows').

Cornell states the second band in the form that makes the mechanism visible: with два, три and четыре the noun must be in the genitive singular. That is why a learner who knows the genitive singular from lesson 53 already has the whole pattern, and why the ending on стола is not a special numeral ending but the ordinary genitive of стол. The same page gives the exception that matters for counting people: when the numeral is in an oblique case, the genitive singular rule stops applying and the noun goes into the plural of that same case. Он купил двадцать два учебника (on koo-PEEL DVAT-tsat dva oo-CHEB-nee-ka, 'he bought twenty-two textbooks') has the genitive singular because the numeral is accusative and the noun is inanimate. Он купил около двадцати двух учебников (a-KA-la dvat-tsa-TEE dvookh oo-CHEB-nee-kaf, 'he bought about twenty-two textbooks') has the genitive plural because около put the numeral into the genitive.

Compound numerals follow the last word, not the first. двадцать один стол is singular because the last word is один; двадцать две книги is feminine because the last word is две; двадцать пять столов is genitive plural because the last word is пять. This is the rule that produces the odd sequence a learner hears in a shop: двадцать один год, двадцать два года, двадцать пять лет. The noun changes three times in three numbers, and the numeral's last word is the only thing deciding.

Adjectives follow the noun band rather than the numeral. With two to four and a masculine or neuter noun, the adjective is genitive plural: два больших стола (DVA bal-SHEEKH sta-LA, 'two big tables'). With two to four and a feminine noun, the adjective is nominative plural: две новые книги (dvye NO-vy-ye KNEE-gee, 'two new books'). With five and above, the adjective is genitive plural: пять хороших книг (pyat kha-RO-sheekh kneek, 'five good books'). Once the numeral is oblique, the adjective simply agrees with the noun in case and number, which Cornell's page on higher numerals states explicitly: с двумя молодыми учительницами (z dvo-MYA ma-la-DY-mee oo-CHEE-tyel-nee-tsa-mee, 'with two young female teachers').

The numerals themselves decline, and the irregular ones are worth memorising as a small set. сорок, девяносто and сто have only two forms: сорок and сорока, девяносто and девяноста, сто and ста. The fifties to eighties are compounds in which both halves decline: пятьдесят, пятидесяти, пятьюдесятью. The hundreds decline in both parts: двести, двухсот, двумстам, двумястами. тысяча is a noun, not a numeral, so it declines like a feminine noun and takes a genitive after it: тысяча рублей, около тысячи рублей.
lessons.example:
Read a column of quantities aloud and listen to the noun change while the number stays recognisable. One item: один стол, одна книга, одно окно. Two: два стола, две книги, два окна. Five: пять столов, пять книг, пять окон. Then the compound series that catches everyone: двадцать один стол, двадцать две книги, двадцать пять столов. Say the three aloud in sequence and notice that the numeral's first word never changes while the noun changes twice.

Now put the same quantities into an oblique case and watch the whole phrase re-shape. Nominative: двадцать два учебника. Genitive after около: около двадцати двух учебников. Instrumental after с: с двадцатью двумя учебниками (z dvat-tsa-TYU dvoo-MYA oo-CHEB-nee-ka-mee, 'with twenty-two textbooks'). Dative after к: к двадцати двум учебникам (k dvat-tsa-TEE dvoom oo-CHEB-nee-kam). Every word in the phrase declines, and the noun is plural in all three oblique examples, which is the point Cornell makes about the genitive singular rule not surviving outside the nominative and accusative.

Finally a sentence with a quantity, an adjective and an oblique numeral, which is where the pattern either holds or collapses. В прошлом году мы работали с двумя новыми поставщиками и получили скидку около пятидесяти процентов (f PROSH-lam ga-DOO my ra-BO-ta-lee z dvo-MYA NO-vy-mee pas-TAF-shee-ka-mee ee pa-loo-CHEE-lee O-ka-la pee-tee-dee-sya-TEE pra-TSEN-taf SKEET-kee, 'last year we worked with two new suppliers and received about fifty per cent discount'). The first numeral is instrumental and its adjective and noun are instrumental plural; the second is genitive after около and its noun is genitive plural. Nothing in the sentence is a special numeral form except the numerals themselves.
lessons.question: You want to say 'about five hundred people work in the plant' and produce «около пятьсот человек работают на заводе». What has gone wrong, and what should it be?
lessons.answer: около governs the genitive, so the numeral must decline to пятисот and the verb then agrees with the quantity as a singular neuter or with the people as plural depending on the intended reading: «около пятисот человек работает на заводе» is the neutral version.
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong, because человек has no plural form after numerals and the numeral пятьсот can stay in the nominative after около.
lessons.correction: The noun is indeed invariable in this counting use, but the numeral is not. около is a genitive preposition, and every word it governs goes into the genitive: около пятисот (O-ka-la pee-tee-SOT). The numeral пятьсот declines in both parts, so the genitive is пятисот, not пятьсот with an ending added somewhere. The distracter confuses the invariability of человек in counting with invariability of the whole phrase, which is a different claim. Compare the nominative пятьсот человек with the genitive около пятисот человек: the noun looks identical and the numeral does not. This is why figures in a report have to be checked word by word rather than sign by sign.

depth.definitions: A cardinal numeral is a number word used for counting, as opposed to an ordinal, which ranks. Government is the relation in which one word requires a particular case in another, and numerals govern the noun that follows them. The genitive singular is the form of a noun meaning 'of one', as in стола or книги; the genitive plural is the form meaning 'of many', as in столов or книг. An oblique case is any case other than the nominative, and in this lesson it is the trigger for the plural noun. A compound numeral is a number written as several words, such as двадцать два, and only its last word governs the noun.
depth.mechanism:
Choose the band by the last word of the numeral, then apply the ending. One: make один agree in gender, number and case. Two to four: genitive singular, with две for feminine nouns. Five and above, including compounds ending in five to twenty, thirty, forty and so on: genitive plural. Then check whether the numeral is in an oblique case, because that overrides the band entirely: if it is, the noun and any adjective go into the plural of that case, which for the genitive is the genitive plural.

The adjective follows the noun, not the numeral, but with one wrinkle. In the two-to-four band, masculine and neuter nouns take a genitive plural adjective and feminine nouns take a nominative plural adjective. That is why два больших стола and две новые книги look as if they follow different rules; they do, and the gender of the noun decides. In the five-plus band there is no wrinkle: genitive plural for both.

Say the compound aloud from the last word backwards. For двадцать два учебника, start at два, hear the genitive singular, and let the двадцать ride along unchanged. For двадцать пять студентов, start at пять, hear the genitive plural, and again let the tens ride. This backwards habit prevents the common error of making the first word agree with the noun.
depth.secondExample:
Take an inventory sentence and change the quantity four times without changing anything else. На складе лежит двадцать один ящик (na SKLA-dee lee-ZHEET DVAT-tsat a-DEEN YE-sheek, 'there are twenty-one boxes in the warehouse'). Change to twenty-two: На складе лежат двадцать два ящика. Change to twenty-five: На складе лежат двадцать пять ящиков. Change to an oblique: На складе не хватает двадцати двух ящиков (na SKLA-dee ne khva-TA-yet dvat-tsa-TEE dvookh YE-shee-kaf, 'the warehouse is short of twenty-two boxes').

The verb agrees with the quantity in the last example, not with the boxes: не хватает is singular because the construction is impersonal and the genitive phrase is its object. That is a separate pattern from numeral agreement, and it is worth noticing because a learner who has just mastered два ящика will try to make the verb agree with ящиков.

Now read the four sentences in sequence and mark the ending of the noun in each: ящик, ящика, ящиков, ящиков. The first is nominative singular, the second genitive singular, the third genitive plural, the fourth genitive plural inside an oblique construction. Four quantities, three noun forms, and the numeral is the only word that tells you which one.
depth.mistake:
The first error is using the nominative after any numeral above one, as in два книга or пять стол. It comes from languages where the plural is the default after a number, and it is repaired by the band rule: two to four genitive singular, five and up genitive plural.

The second error is making the first word of a compound numeral govern the noun, as in двадцать два книга or двадцать пять стола. The repair is to read the numeral backwards from its last word.

The third error is leaving the numeral in the nominative after a preposition, as in около пять человек or с двадцать учебники. The repair is to decline every word in the phrase, which for the hundreds means both halves: около пятисот, с двумястами.

A fourth error belongs to learners who have over-generalised the feminine form две and use it with masculine nouns, producing две стола. The gender split is only in the numeral two, and it follows the noun: две книги, два стола, две недели, два дня.
depth.application:
Write an inventory of one room in your home or office with ten lines, each using a different numeral band: one item, two items, three, four, five, ten, twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-five, and one line with около plus a numeral. Read the list aloud and stop at every noun to say which band it belongs to.

Then convert five of the lines to an oblique case by putting с, около or к in front, and read them again. The numerals will decline and the nouns will move to the plural, and the exercise is finished when you can do that without stopping to think about the band.

Finally write two sentences about your team with двадцать два and около двадцати двух, and check the verb agreement in each. The difference between the two sentences is the whole lesson in miniature.
depth.summary: один agrees like an adjective; два to четыре take the genitive singular, with две for feminine nouns; пять and above take the genitive plural. A compound numeral is governed by its last word, and an oblique numeral puts the noun into the plural of that case. Adjectives follow the noun band, with a feminine exception in the two-to-four range. The numerals themselves decline, and the irregular set сорок, девяносто and сто has only two forms.

lessons.title: Counting what has no singular: сутки, дети, and the collective numerals
lessons.explanation:
The counting rule from lesson 116 assumes that a noun has a singular to put into the genitive. A small set of nouns does not. деньги (DYEN-gee, 'money'), часы (cha-SY, 'clock, watch'), сутки (SOOT-kee, 'twenty-four hours'), брюки (BRYOO-kee, 'trousers'), очки (ach-KEE, 'glasses'), каникулы (ka-NEE-koo-ly, 'school holidays'), ворота (va-RO-ta, 'gate') and ножницы (NOZH-nee-tsy, 'scissors') exist only in the plural, and дети (DYE-tee, 'children') is the plural of ребёнок (ree-BYO-nak, 'child') with no singular of its own. Cornell draws the consequence in one sentence: for such nouns the genitive singular rule cannot apply, so you use a collective numeral with the noun in the genitive plural.

The collective numerals are двое (DVO-ye, 'two of'), трое (TRO-ye, 'three of'), четверо (CHYET-vee-ra, 'four of'), пятеро, шестеро, семеро and so on. They are used in three situations. First, with plural-only nouns, where the ordinary two-to-four rule has nothing to work with: двое суток (DVO-ye SOO-tak, 'two days and nights'), трое часов (TRO-ye cha-SOF, 'three watches'), двое очков (DVO-ye ach-KOF, 'two pairs of glasses'). Second, with masculine nouns denoting people, where they add a nuance of 'a group of': двое мужчин (DVO-ye moosh-CHEEN, 'two men'), трое друзей (TRO-ye droo-ZYEY, 'three friends'), четверо коллег. Third, in the predicate with a pronoun: нас двое (nas DVO-ye, 'there are two of us'), их трое (eekh TRO-ye, 'there are three of them').

Two limits are absolute. Collective numerals do not combine with feminine nouns that denote women: two women is две женщины (dvye ZHEN-shee-ny), never двое женщин. And they do not combine with inanimate masculine nouns that have a normal singular: two tables is два стола, not двое столов. The collective is for groups of people and for nouns that have no singular, and outside those two uses it sounds wrong rather than merely bookish.

Above four, the ordinary numerals return with the genitive plural, because there is no genitive singular problem once the noun is plural anyway. пять суток (PYAT SOO-tak, 'five days and nights'), пять часов (PYAT cha-SOF, 'five watches' or 'five o'clock'), шесть детей (shest dye-TYEY, 'six children'). The ladder is therefore: one takes the bare noun or the plural form одни, which is why сутки alone means 'a day and a night' while одни сутки often adds the sense of 'exactly one', two to four take a collective, five and up take the ordinary numeral with the genitive plural.

Three suppletive nouns need to be learned as sets because no rule produces them. год (got, 'year') has the genitive singular года and the genitive plural лет: один год, два года, пять лет, двадцать один год, двадцать два года, тридцать лет. человек (chee-la-VYEK, 'person') has the counting genitive plural человек, identical to the nominative singular, while the ordinary plural is люди (LYU-dee, 'people'): один человек, два человека, пять человек, много людей. ребёнок has ребёнка in the genitive singular and детей in the plural: один ребёнок, два ребёнка, пятеро детей.

деньги behaves the same way and produces some of the most useful phrases in the language. 'A lot of money' is много денег (MNO-ga DYE-nek), 'no money' is нет денег (nyet DYE-nek), and 'small change' is мелкие деньги (MYEL-kee-ye DYEN-gee). When you need to count, you count the objects rather than the mass: монета (ma-NYE-ta, 'coin') and купюра (koo-PYOO-ra, 'banknote') have ordinary singulars and take the ordinary ladder, which is why две монеты and пять купюр are regular while двое денег is not a phrase at all.

Agreement with these quantities is worth one sentence. A collective numeral with a plural-only noun usually takes a plural verb when the noun is the subject: Двое детей играют во дворе (DVO-ye dye-TYEY ee-GRA-yoo-oot va dvo-RYE, 'two children are playing in the yard'). When the same phrase measures duration, the verb is neuter singular: Прошло двое суток (prah-SHLO DVO-ye SOO-tak, 'two days and nights passed'). The noun does not change; the construction does.
lessons.example:
Read a set of quantities built on nouns without singulars and watch the numeral do the work. Two days and nights: двое суток. Three watches: трое часов. Two pairs of glasses: двое очков. Five days and nights: пять суток. Two children: двое детей, or два ребёнка if you are counting children rather than a group. Five children: пятеро детей or пять детей, and the first sounds like a family, the second like a register.

Now the year and age set, which every learner needs in conversation. Мне двадцать один год (mnye DVAT-tsat a-DEEN got, 'I am twenty-one'). Мне двадцать два года. Мне двадцать пять лет. Моему сыну три года, а дочери шесть лет (ma-yee-MOO SY-noo tree GO-da, a DO-chee-ree shest lyet, 'my son is three and my daughter is six'). Notice that the noun changes from год to года to лет while the meaning of 'year' never changes, and that the choice is decided by the last word of the numeral.

Now a paragraph that mixes all three types. В отделе работают двадцать два человека, из них пятеро мужчин и семнадцать женщин (f at-DYE-lee ra-BO-ta-yoot DVAT-tsat dva chee-la-VYE-ka, eez neekh PYA-tee-ra moosh-CHEEN ee see-MNAT-tsat ZHYEN-shcheen, 'twenty-two people work in the department, five of them men and seventeen women'). Проект длился трое суток, и на командировку ушло пять суток (pra-YEKT dleel-SYA TRO-ye SOO-tak, ee na ka-man-dee-ROF-koo oosh-LO PYAT SOO-tak, 'the project lasted three days and nights, and five days went on the trip'). The first sentence uses a normal counted noun, человек, in the genitive singular after два; the second uses a collective with a plural-only noun; the third uses the ordinary numeral with the genitive plural.
lessons.question: You want to say 'the trip took two days' and produce «командировка заняла два суток». What is wrong, and what should it be?
lessons.answer: сутки has no singular, so the two-to-four band cannot produce a genitive singular from it; the form is the collective with the genitive plural: «командировка заняла двое суток». If you mean two ordinary days, say «два дня».
lessons.distractor: The sentence is correct, because два is the numeral for two and суток is already the genitive plural, which is what numerals above one require.
lessons.correction: The noun form суток is right and the numeral is wrong, which is why the error is easy to miss. The two-to-four band does not take the genitive plural; it takes the genitive singular, and сутки has none. Russian solves this with the collective двое, which is built for exactly this gap: двое суток. The distracter applies the five-and-above rule to a two, which produces a phrase that looks plausible and is not said. The same repair gives двое часов for two watches, and the contrast with два часа, two hours, is the clearest proof that the collective is doing grammatical work rather than adding style.

depth.definitions: A plural-only noun is a noun that has no singular forms, such as сутки or деньги; English has the same category in 'scissors' and 'trousers'. A collective numeral is a numeral meaning 'a group of', such as двое or трое, which takes the genitive plural and is restricted to plural-only nouns and to masculine persons. Suppletion is the use of different roots for forms of one word, as in человек and люди, or год and лет. The counting form is the genitive plural used after numerals, which for человек is человек and for год is лет.
depth.mechanism:
Decide first whether the noun has a singular. If it does, use the ordinary ladder from lesson 116. If it does not, the two-to-four band is filled by a collective numeral plus the genitive plural, and the five-plus band is filled by an ordinary numeral plus the genitive plural, which means the noun looks the same in both bands and only the numeral changes: двое суток against пять суток.

Then check whether the noun denotes people. If it denotes men, the collective is available in the two-to-four band and adds the sense of a group: двое мужчин, трое коллег. If it denotes women, the collective is unavailable and the ordinary numeral is used with the nominative plural, which is the feminine pattern from lesson 116: две женщины, три женщины. If it denotes things with a normal singular, the collective is unavailable too: два стола, not двое столов.

The suppletive nouns are learned as three-line sets and drilled with the last-word rule. For year: год, года, лет. For person: человек, человека, человек. For child: ребёнок, ребёнка, детей. In each set, the middle form serves the two-to-four band and the last form serves five and above, and the last form is the one that also appears in the oblique plural.
depth.secondExample:
Take a staffing sentence and rebuild it three ways to show what the collective adds. Neutral count: В команде двадцать два человека (f ka-MAN-dee DVAT-tsat dva chee-la-VYE-ka, 'there are twenty-two people in the team'). Group reading of a small subset: В команде двое новых сотрудников (f ka-MAN-dee DVO-ye NO-vykh sa-TROOD-nee-kaf, 'there are two new employees in the team'). Feminine subset, where the collective is impossible: В команде две новые сотрудницы (f ka-MAN-dee dvye NO-vy-ye sa-TROOD-nee-tsy, 'there are two new female employees in the team').

Now a duration paragraph. Поездка заняла двое суток, обратная дорога ещё сутки, а всего мы были в пути трое суток (pa-YEZ-dka za-ny a-LA DVO-ye SOO-tak, a-BRAT-na-ya da-RO-ga yesh-SHYO SOOT-kee, a fsye-VO my BY-lee f poo-TEE TRO-ye SOO-tak, 'the trip took two days and nights, the return journey another day, and in total we were on the road three days and nights'). Every quantity here is built on сутки, and the numerals are двое and трое because the noun has no singular. A learner who says два суток will be understood and will sound wrong, which is the worst combination for a professional register.
depth.mistake:
The first error is два суток, three words that look right and are not. The repair is to hear the missing singular and switch to the collective: двое суток.

The second error is the collective with a feminine noun, двое женщин or трое девушек. The repair is the ordinary feminine numeral: две женщины, три девушки. The restriction is grammatical rather than polite, and it applies to the numeral, not to the people.

The third error is the invented genitive plural человеков. человек has no such form; the counting genitive plural is человек, and the ordinary plural is люди. The repair is to memorise пять человек and много людей as two different phrases with two different jobs.

A fourth error is the year set, where learners produce пять годов or два лет. The repair is the three-line set год, года, лет, drilled with the numbers one, two and five until the sequence is automatic. Note that лет is also the form used in ages, so Мне тридцать лет is the same word as the one in тридцать лет работы.
depth.application:
Describe your household or your team in six lines, using at least two plural-only nouns and at least two collective numerals. For example: У нас двое детей, им пять и восемь лет. В офисе двое новых сотрудников и три новых сотрудницы. Поезд идёт двое суток. На отпуск у меня осталось пять дней. (oo nas DVO-ye dye-TYEY, eem PYAT ee VO-seem lyet. v OF-ee-see DVO-ye NO-vykh sa-TROOD-nee-kaf ee tree NO-vykh sa-TROOD-nee-tsy. PO-yest ee-DYOT DVO-ye SOO-tak. na OT-poosk oo mee-NYA as-TA-las PYAT dyey. 'We have two children, aged five and eight. The office has two new male employees and three new female employees. The train takes two days and nights. I have five days left for holiday.')

Then take three of the lines and say them with a different quantity: change двое детей to трое детей, then to пять детей; change двое суток to трое суток, then to пять суток. Say each aloud and check that the noun form changes only when the numeral crosses into a different band.

Finish with a two-line comparison that uses both два and двое with the same root, such as два часа against двое часов, and explain aloud what each one counts. If you can say why the second phrase needs the collective, the lesson is finished.
depth.summary: Nouns without singulars take a collective numeral in the two-to-four band and an ordinary numeral with the genitive plural above four: двое суток, пять суток. Collectives also serve masculine persons and pronoun predicates, but never feminine nouns or ordinary countable things. год, человек and ребёнок are suppletive sets, and the last word of a compound numeral chooses the form.

lessons.title: Dates and months: naming a day, locating an event, and the year in the prepositional
lessons.explanation:
A date in Russian has two shapes, and the difference between them is the difference between naming and locating. Naming the day, as you do when someone asks what today's date is, uses the nominative: Сегодня второе февраля (see-VO-dnya fta-RO-ye feev-ra-LYA, 'today is the second of February'). Locating an event on that day uses the genitive: Мы встретились второго февраля (my FSTRYE-tee-lees fta-RO-va feev-ra-LYA, 'we met on the second of February'). The month is genitive in both, because the day is 'the second of February' in either construction. Only the ordinal changes, and it changes because the question changed: Какое сегодня число? (KA-ko-ye see-VO-dnya chee-SLO, 'what is the date today?') asks for a nominative, Какого числа? (ka-KO-va chee-SLA, 'on what date?') asks for a genitive.

The month is the stable part of the date and it is always genitive after the day: пятого марта (PYA-ta-va MAR-ta, 'on the fifth of March'), двадцать третьего апреля (DVAT-tsat TRYET-ye-va ap-RYE-lya, 'on the twenty-third of April'). That is why the month list has to be learned in the genitive first, and only then in the other cases. The twelve genitives are января, февраля, марта, апреля, мая, июня, июля, августа, сентября, октября, ноября, декабря (yeen-va-RYA, feev-ra-LYA, MAR-ta, ap-RYE-lya, MA-ya, ee-YOO-nya, ee-YOO-lya, AV-goo-sta, seen-TYAB-rya, ak-TYAB-rya, na-YAB-rya, dee-KAB-rya).

The other cases are needed as soon as you say anything more than a date. 'In January' is в январе (v yeen-va-RYE), prepositional. 'By January' is к январю (k yeen-va-RYOO), dative. 'Until January' is до января (da yeen-va-RYA), genitive. 'From January to March' is с января по март (s yeen-va-RYA pa MART), genitive then accusative, and the по here means 'through' rather than 'to', so the end point is included. 'January' as the subject or the object is январь (yeen-VAR), and 'with January' is январём (yeen-va-RYOM), instrumental.

The instrumental is where the spelling splits and the stress decides. Masculine months in -ь take -ем when the stress stays on the stem and -ём when it moves to the ending: апрель gives апрелем (ap-RYE-lem, stress on the stem), while январь gives январём, февраль gives февралём, сентябрь gives сентябрём, and the same pattern runs through октябрь, ноябрь and декабрь. Months in -й and the hard-stem months take -ом or -ем: май gives маем (MA-yeem), август gives августом (AV-goo-stam), март gives мартом (MAR-tam). The rule is not a month rule at all; it is the ordinary instrumental rule for masculine nouns, and the months simply obey it.

Years add a second declension. The word год is masculine and takes году in the prepositional, with the stress on the ending: в прошлом году (f PROSH-lam ga-DOO, 'last year'), в этом году (v E-tam ga-DOO, 'this year'), в следующем году (f SLYE-doo-yoo-shchem ga-DOO, 'next year'). A specific year is an ordinal numeral in the prepositional plus году: в две тысячи двадцать седьмом году (v DVYE TY-see-chee DVAT-tsat seed-MOM ga-DOO, 'in the year 2027'). In a compound ordinal only the last word declines, which is why две тысячи and двадцать stay in their dictionary shape while седьмом carries the case.

Two smaller facts complete the picture. Ordinals decline as adjectives, and the only irregular one in the date range is третий, whose genitive is третьего (TRYET-ye-va) and whose neuter is третье. And a date range is built with с plus the genitive and по plus the accusative: с первого по пятое мая (s PYER-va-va pa PYA-ta-ye MA-ya, 'from the first to the fifth of May, inclusive'). If you want the range to exclude the last day, до plus the genitive does that: с первого до пятого мая.
lessons.example:
Read a diary paragraph and label the case of every date. Третьего марта мы подписали договор (TRYET-ye-va MAR-ta my pad-pee-SA-lee da-ga-VOR, 'on the third of March we signed the contract'). The date is genitive because it locates the event. В апреле начнётся поставка (v ap-RYE-lee nach-NYOT-sya pa-STAF-ka, 'the delivery begins in April'). The month is prepositional because it is a location in time. К маю мы закончим первый этап (k MA-yoo my za-KON-cheem PYER-vy ee-TAP, 'by May we will finish the first stage'). The month is dative because к governs the dative. С января по март мы работали над проектом (s yeen-va-RYA pa MART my ra-BO-ta-lee nat pra-YEKT-am, 'from January through March we worked on the project'). The first month is genitive after с, the second is accusative after по.

Now the same paragraph with years. Договор подписан пятого марта две тысячи двадцать седьмого года (da-ga-VOR PAT-pee-san PYA-ta-va MAR-ta DVYE TY-see-chee DVAT-tsat seed-MO-va GO-da, 'the contract was signed on the fifth of March 2027'). Both the day and the year are genitive, and the month sits between them in the genitive as well. Three genitives in a row, which is what a full date looks like in Russian.

Then a sentence that names rather than locates, as a receptionist would say it. Сегодня пятое марта, а завтра будет шестое (see-VO-dnya PYA-ta-ye MAR-ta, a ZAF-tra BOO-det shes-TO-ye, 'today is the fifth of March and tomorrow will be the sixth'). The day is nominative, the month is genitive, and the verb будет is optional in the present but normal in the future.
lessons.question: You are writing a notice and produce «Собрание состоится в второе марта». What is wrong, and what should it be?
lessons.answer: A date that locates an event takes the genitive, and the preposition в is not used with a bare date: «Собрание состоится второго марта».
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong, because в marks the time of an event and второе марта is the correct accusative form after в.
lessons.correction: в does mark time, but it takes the prepositional for months and hours (в марте, в три часа), not the accusative for a calendar date. A date on which something happens is a genitive phrase with no preposition at all: второго марта. The distracter has understood that в is a time preposition and has not learned which case it wants with which kind of time expression, which is the central confusion of this lesson. The repair is to ask whether the time expression is a date (genitive, no preposition), a month (prepositional with в), a clock time (accusative with в) or a duration (accusative with no preposition).

depth.definitions: An ordinal numeral ranks, as in первый, второй, третий, and it declines like an adjective. A cardinal numeral counts, as in один, два, три. Naming a date presents it as a fact about the calendar; locating an event presents the date as the time of something else, and Russian marks the two with nominative and genitive respectively. The month names form a closed set of twelve nouns, and the year is expressed either by год with a cardinal numeral or by an ordinal numeral agreeing with году.
depth.mechanism:
Build a date in three slots: day, month, year. The day is an ordinal, nominative when you name the date and genitive when you locate an event. The month is always genitive after the day, whatever the day's case. The year, if you give one, is a genitive ordinal plus года, or a prepositional ordinal plus году when the year is the location rather than part of the date.

Choose the month's case by the preposition or by its job. No preposition and a locating function gives the genitive. в gives the prepositional for a month and the accusative for a clock time. к gives the dative. до and с give the genitive. по gives the accusative when it marks an inclusive end point. The instrumental appears with с in the sense of 'with' and in a few fixed phrases, and it is the case that shows whether the stress has moved to the ending.

For the year, decide whether it is a label or a location. A label takes the nominative: две тысячи двадцать седьмой год. A location takes в plus the prepositional: в две тысячи двадцать седьмом году. A boundary takes с or до plus the genitive: с две тысячи двадцать седьмого года, до две тысячи двадцать седьмого года. Only the final word of the ordinal changes in each case, and the words before it stay put.
depth.secondExample:
Read a short news item and check every time expression. Пятого февраля две тысячи двадцать седьмого года компания объявила о новом проекте (PYA-ta-va feev-ra-LYA DVYE TY-see-chee DVAT-tsat seed-MO-va GO-da kam-PA-nee-ya ab-yee-VEE-la a NO-vam pra-YEKT-ye, 'on the fifth of February 2027 the company announced a new project'). The date is a chain of genitives, and the verb объявила governs о plus the prepositional for the thing announced. В марте начнутся поставки, а к июню проект выйдет на полную мощность (v MAR-tye nach-NOOT-sya pa-STAF-kee, a k ee-YOO-nyoo pra-YEKT VY-deet na POL-noo-yoo MOSHCH-nast, 'in March deliveries will begin, and by June the project will reach full capacity').

The first sentence dates the announcement, the second locates the deliveries in a month and sets a deadline with к. Three different time cases in two sentences, and none of them is the nominative, because none of them is naming a date. That is the distribution you should expect in news prose: the genitive for when something happened, the prepositional for the month it happens in, the dative for the deadline.
depth.mistake:
The most common error is в plus a date, as in в второе марта, which mixes the prepositional pattern for months with the bare genitive pattern for dates. The repair is to drop в and put the day into the genitive.

The second error is a nominative month after a genitive day, as in пятого март. The month's case is decided by the date construction, not by the day's case, and it is genitive in every date: пятого марта.

The third error is a nominative year after в, as in в две тысячи двадцать седьмой год. в requires the prepositional for a year, so the ordinal becomes седьмом and год becomes году: в две тысячи двадцать седьмом году. The repair is to hear году as a single unit and to change the ordinal to match it.

A fourth error is the wrong day form for a feminine-looking date. All dates use the neuter ordinal, because the understood noun is число, which is neuter: пятое марта, not пятая марта. Learners who are thinking of дата, which is feminine, produce the feminine form, and the understood noun in the construction is число.
depth.application:
Write your calendar for the next three months with one line per month: two dates, one month phrase with в, one deadline with к, and one range with с plus по. For example: Пятого марта встреча. В апреле отпуск. К маю закончить отчёт. С первого по десятое июня командировка. (PYA-ta-va MAR-ta FSTRYE-cha. v ap-RYE-lee OT-poosk. k MA-yoo za-KON-cheet at-CHYOT. s PYER-va-va pa dee-SYA-ta-ye ee-YOO-nya ka-man-dee-ROF-ka. 'Meeting on the fifth of March. Holiday in April. Finish the report by May. Business trip from the first to the tenth of June.')

Read the eight lines aloud and check the case of every month and every ordinal. Then add one year to two of the dates and read them again, once as a label and once as a location, so that седьмой год and седьмом году are both said in the same minute.

Finish by answering three questions aloud: Какое сегодня число? Какого числа вы начали работать? В каком году вы родились? The three answers use three different cases, and saying them in sequence is the fastest way to feel the distribution.
depth.summary: A date is an ordinal plus a genitive month, and the ordinal is nominative when it names the day and genitive when it locates an event. Months take the prepositional after в, the dative after к, the genitive after с and до, and the accusative after по for an inclusive end. Years use году in the prepositional and only the last word of a compound ordinal declines. All dates use the neuter ordinal, because the understood noun is число.

lessons.title: Clock time and duration: который час, в котором часу, через and назад
lessons.explanation:
Russian time talk runs on four different questions, and each one takes a different construction. Который час? (ka-TO-ryy CHAS, 'what time is it?') asks for the clock reading. В котором часу? (f ka-TO-ram cha-SOO, 'at what time?') asks for a point in the day. Сколько времени? (SKOL-ka VRYE-mee-nee) asks 'how much time?' when it has a verb with it, and it asks 'what time is it?' when it stands alone, which is an ambiguity worth knowing rather than a rule to fix. Во сколько? (va SKOL-ka, 'at what time?') is the colloquial version of the second question, and it is what most people actually say.

The clock reading has two registers. The easy one names the hour and then the minutes in sequence, as a digital display does: восемь пятнадцать (VO-seem peet-NAT-tsat, '8:15'). A timetable, an announcement board or a control room uses this form, and it is also what you say when the exact minute matters more than the elegance of the phrase. The traditional one counts the minutes of the hour that is coming: пять минут первого (PYAT mee-NOOT PYER-va-va, literally 'five minutes of the first [hour]', meaning 12:05), четверть шестого (CHYET-vert shes-TO-va, 'a quarter of the sixth', meaning 5:15), половина шестого (pa-la-VEE-na shes-TO-va, 'half of the sixth', meaning 5:30). The ordinal is genitive because the minutes belong to the hour: the fifth minute of the sixth hour, not the fifth minute after five.

The trap is половина шестого. English speakers hear 'half past five' and produce половина пятого, which means 4:30. Russian counts the hour that is in progress, so half of the sixth hour is 5:30, and half of the fifth hour is 4:30. The same logic makes четверть шестого 5:15 and без четверти шесть 5:45. Once you accept that the ordinal names the hour being counted towards, the whole system becomes regular.

The left side of the clock uses без plus the genitive: без пяти три (byes pee-TEE tree, 'five to three', 2:55), без четверти три (byes CHYET-ver-tee tree, 2:45), без двадцати пяти восемь (byes DVAT-tsat-ee pee-TEE VO-seem, 7:35). The hour after без stays in the nominative, because it is the hour you are approaching rather than the hour you are in.

To say at what time, use в plus the accusative for the hour and the minutes: в три часа (f tree cha-SA, 'at three o'clock'), в пять минут первого (f PYAT mee-NOOT PYER-va-va, 'at five past twelve'). The half hour is the exception that proves the case system: в половине шестого (f pa-la-VEE-nee shes-TO-va), with the prepositional, because половина is a noun and в locates inside it. The colloquial alternative is в полшестого (f pal-shes-TO-va), which avoids the ending entirely.

Durations take the accusative with no preposition: два часа (DVA cha-SA, 'two hours'), пять минут, полтора часа (pal-ta-RA cha-SA, 'an hour and a half'), трое суток. The verb длиться takes the same accusative: Собрание длилось два часа (sa-BRA-nee-ye DLEE-las DVA cha-SA, 'the meeting lasted two hours'). Offsets use через plus the accusative for 'in' and назад plus the accusative for 'ago': через час (CHYE-res CHAS, 'in an hour'), час назад (CHAS na-ZAT, 'an hour ago'), через два дня, два дня назад. Spans use с plus the genitive and до plus the genitive, or по plus the accusative for an inclusive end: с двух до четырёх (z dvooh da chee-ty-RYOKH, 'from two to four'), с понедельника по среду (s pa-nee-DYEL-nee-ka pa SRYE-doo, 'from Monday through Wednesday').

One pair decides whether you have understood the aspect lessons. Я читал книгу два часа (ya chee-TAL KNEE-goo DVA cha-SA, 'I read the book for two hours') describes the activity and says nothing about finishing it. Я прочитал книгу за два часа (ya pra-chee-TAL KNEE-goo za DVA cha-SA, 'I read the book in two hours') describes a completed result and measures the time it took. The accusative alone measures duration; за plus the accusative measures the time within which something was completed. A perfective verb with a bare accusative duration is the error that follows from ignoring this pair.
lessons.example:
Read a timetable aloud in the traditional register and check every ordinal. Поезд уходит в семь минут девятого (PO-yest oo-KHO-deet f syem mee-NOOT dee-VYA-ta-va, 'the train leaves at 8:07'). The meeting starts at a quarter past ten: Собрание начинается в четверть одиннадцатого (sa-BRA-nee-ye na-chee-NA-yet-sya f CHYET-vert a-dee-NAT-tsa-ta-va). The call is at half past six: Звонок в половине седьмого (zva-NOK f pa-la-VEE-nee seed-MO-va). The plane lands at twenty to nine: Самолёт садится без двадцати девять (sa-ma-LYOT sa-DEET-sya byes DVAT-tsat-ee DYE-veet).

Now a paragraph of durations and offsets. Дорога заняла два часа. Мы выехали через полчаса после завтрака и вернулись через час. (da-RO-ga za-ny a-LA DVA cha-SA. my VY-ye-ha-lee CHYE-res pal-cha-SA PO-sle ZAF-tra-ka ee veer-NOO-lees CHYE-res CHAS.) 'The journey took two hours. We set off half an hour after breakfast and came back an hour later.' Note заняла with the accusative duration, выехали with через for the offset after an event, and вернулись with через for the offset before the return.

Now the aspect pair in one minute. Я готовил отчёт три часа, но так и не закончил (ya ga-TO-veel at-CHYOT tree cha-SA, no tak ee ne za-KON-cheel, 'I worked on the report for three hours and never finished it'). Я подготовил отчёт за три часа (ya pad-ga-TO-veel at-CHYOT za tree cha-SA, 'I prepared the report in three hours'). The first is imperfective with a bare duration and admits failure; the second is perfective with за and asserts completion. The time expressions are not interchangeable, and the choice of verb is what makes each one true.
lessons.question: A colleague asks «В котором часу начинается встреча?» and you answer «В половине шестого». What time have you given, and what would a learner who says «в половине пятого» be saying?
lessons.answer: You have given 5:30. Половина шестого is half of the sixth hour, so the learner who says в половине пятого is saying 4:30, not 5:30.
lessons.distractor: Both phrases mean 5:30, because половина is 'half' and the ordinal only agrees with the hour that has already passed.
lessons.correction: The ordinal names the hour being counted towards, so шестого means the sixth hour is in progress and its half is 5:30. в половине пятого is half of the fifth hour, which is 4:30, and it is a real appointment an hour earlier than intended. The distracter assumes the ordinal refers back to the hour that has passed, which is the English pattern of 'half past five'. The repair is to translate the phrase literally once, 'half of the sixth hour', and then to stop translating it. Note also that в половине takes the prepositional, not the accusative, because половина is a noun and the time is located inside it.

depth.definitions: Clock time is a point in the day, expressed in Russian either digitally or by counting minutes of the coming hour. Duration is a length of time, expressed with the accusative and no preposition. An offset is a distance from a reference point, expressed with через for a point after it and назад for a point before it. A span is a stretch with two ends, expressed with с plus the genitive and до plus the genitive, or по plus the accusative when the second end is included. The aspect pair imperfective with a bare duration against perfective with за plus the accusative distinguishes time spent from time taken to finish.
depth.mechanism:
Choose the question first, because the question fixes the construction. Который час takes a clock reading: minutes plus the genitive ordinal of the coming hour, or the digital form. В котором часу takes в plus the accusative of the hour, with the half hour as the prepositional exception. Сколько времени with a verb takes the accusative of duration. Во сколько takes в plus the accusative, like the second question.

Then place the offset relative to the event. If the event is in the future, use через plus the accusative and count forward from now: через два часа. If the event is in the past, use назад plus the accusative and count backward: два часа назад. Do not combine them, because через and назад point in opposite directions and a phrase with both is not a phrase.

For a span, decide whether the second end is included. с понедельника до среды stops on Wednesday morning; с понедельника по среду includes Wednesday. The first uses до plus the genitive, the second по plus the accusative, and the difference is a working day.

Finally check the aspect. If the verb is perfective, the time expression should normally be за plus the accusative, because a perfective verb presents a completed result and за measures the time it took. If the verb is imperfective, the bare accusative measures how long the activity went on. A perfective verb with a bare accusative is the mismatch to listen for.
depth.secondExample:
Read a travel day and label every time expression by type. Поезд отправляется в семь минут девятого, и дорога занимает два часа (PO-yest at-prav-LYA-yet-sya f syem mee-NOOT dee-VYA-ta-va, ee da-RO-ga za-nee-MA-yet DVA cha-SA, 'the train leaves at 8:07 and the journey takes two hours'). The first is a clock point, the second a duration. Мы приехали за десять минут до отправления (my pree-YE-ha-lee za DYE-seet mee-NOOT da at-prav-LYE-nee-ya, 'we arrived ten minutes before departure'). за here measures the margin, and до plus the genitive names the reference point. Обратно мы ехали полтора часа и вернулись через сутки (a-BRAT-na my YE-ha-lee pal-ta-RA cha-SA ee veer-NOO-lees CHYE-res SOOT-kee, 'we travelled back for an hour and a half and returned a day later').

Now the same day in the digital register, which is what a phone screen or an announcement board would give. Поезд отправляется в 8:07, дорога занимает 2 часа, обратно 1,5 часа (VO-seem zero SYEM, DVA cha-SA, pal-ta-RA cha-SA). The information is identical and the register is unmistakable: the traditional form belongs to speech and to careful writing, the digital form to schedules and screens. A learner who can move between them has both registers, which is the goal of this unit.
depth.mistake:
The first error is the half hour, as in в половине пятого for 5:30. The repair is to say the literal phrase once and then to trust it: half of the sixth hour.

The second error is combining через and назад, as in через два часа назад. The repair is to decide the direction before choosing the preposition: forward takes через, backward takes назад.

The third error is the bare accusative with a perfective verb, as in Я прочитал книгу два часа. The repair is за: Я прочитал книгу за два часа. The bare accusative would describe the activity, and the perfective verb cannot describe an activity, only a result.

A fourth error is answering Сколько времени? with a duration when the question was about the clock. The question is genuinely ambiguous without a verb, so the safe answer names the clock when the question stands alone and names the duration when it has a verb: Сколько времени ты ждал? Два часа. Который час? Половина шестого.
depth.application:
Write your morning as a timetable with six clock times, then rewrite it as a paragraph of durations and offsets. For example: Я встаю в семь минут восьмого. Завтрак занимает полчаса. Я выхожу через час после подъёма. Дорога занимает сорок минут. Я прихожу на работу без десяти девять. Обед длится час. (ya fsta-YOO f syem mee-NOOT vas-MO-va. ZAF-trak za-nee-MA-yet pal-cha-SA. ya vy-kha-ZHOO CHYE-res CHAS PO-sle pad-YO-ma. da-RO-ga za-nee-MA-yet SO-rak mee-NOOT. ya pree-kha-ZHOO na ra-BO-too byes dee-see-TEE DYE-veet. a-BYED DLEET-sya CHAS. 'I get up at 7:07. Breakfast takes half an hour. I leave an hour after getting up. The journey takes forty minutes. I arrive at work at ten to nine. Lunch lasts an hour.')

Read the timetable aloud and check that every clock time has the right ordinal, then read the paragraph and check that every duration is accusative and every offset uses через or назад correctly.

Finish with one aspect pair about your own work: a sentence with an imperfective verb and a bare duration, and the same content with a perfective verb and за. Say both aloud and explain which one claims completion.
depth.summary: Который час asks for the clock, в котором часу and во сколько ask for a point, and сколько времени asks for a duration when it has a verb. The traditional clock counts minutes of the coming hour, so половина шестого is 5:30 and без пяти три is 2:55. Durations take the bare accusative, offsets take через or назад plus the accusative, spans take с plus the genitive and до or по, and perfective verbs take за plus the accusative for the time taken.

lessons.title: Prices, figures and fractions: reading a news bulletin aloud
lessons.explanation:
A figure in a Russian news report is not read digit by digit, and it is not read in the case it is written in. It is read as a phrase whose last numeral governs the noun, and then the whole phrase is put into whatever case the word in front of it demands. That is the whole skill of this lesson, and it explains why a reader who knows the numbers from lesson 116 can still stumble on a single sentence of a bulletin. The figures in a report are compounds, they contain decimals, and they sit after prepositions such as около, более and порядка that force the genitive on everything inside them.

Start with money, because money is where the written form and the spoken form diverge most visibly. 80,68 рубля is written with рубля in the genitive singular, because a decimal fraction governs the genitive singular. Read aloud, it becomes восемьдесят рублей шестьдесят восемь копеек (VO-seem-de-seet roob-LYEY shest-de-SYAT VO-seem ka-PYE-yek): eighty rubles and sixty-eight kopecks. The written form abbreviates the phrase, and the spoken form restores the rubles and kopecks as two counted nouns, each taking the form its own numeral requires. The same sentence in Rossiyskaya Gazeta's October 2026 currency report reads 80,68 рубля за доллар, and the bulletin reader says восемьдесят рублей шестьдесят восемь копеек за доллар, with за plus the accusative for the thing one ruble buys.

Prices follow the same logic with a small set of verbs. Цена составляет 80 рублей (tsee-NA sas-tav-LYA-yet VO-seem-de-seet roob-LYEY, 'the price is eighty rubles'). Цена выросла с 80 до 90 рублей (tsee-NA VY-ras-la s VO-seem-de-see-ta da dee-vya-NO-sta roob-LYEY, 'the price rose from eighty to ninety rubles'). Цена выросла на 10 процентов (na DYE-seet pra-TSEN-taf, 'the price rose by ten per cent'). Here с governs the genitive, до governs the genitive, and на governs the accusative for the amount of the change, which is why the same word рублей appears with different numerals in the same sentence and never changes its own ending.

Large figures are read in groups, and the group boundary is the thousand. 29 904 рубля is двадцать девять тысяч девятьсот четыре рубля (DVAT-tsat DYE-veet TY-seech dee-veet-SOT chee-TY-ree roob-LYA), 'twenty-nine thousand nine hundred and four rubles'. The word тысяча is a noun, so it takes the genitive plural тысяч after девять, and the final group ends in четыре, which forces рубля. The pension figure in Rossiyskaya Gazeta's October 2026 budget report is exactly this number, and reading it correctly requires three decisions in one phrase: тысяч after девять, девятьсот as a compound hundred, and рубля after четыре.

Decimals have their own formula. A number written with a comma is read as whole units plus tenths or hundredths: 6,35 is шесть целых тридцать пять сотых (shest TSE-lykh TREET-tsat pyat SO-tykh, 'six wholes and thirty-five hundredths'). When a noun follows, it is genitive singular, so 6,35 процента is шесть целых тридцать пять сотых процента (pra-TSEN-ta). This is the standard reading of an inflation figure, and it is why a bulletin says процента rather than процентов even though the number is well above four: the decimal, not the integer, governs the noun. 0,11 процента reads ноль целых одиннадцать сотых процента.

Approximation is a set of prepositions with one shared consequence. около, более, менее and порядка all govern the genitive, and they force every numeral inside the phrase into the genitive too. более 100 миллиардов рублей is read более ста миллиардов рублей (BO-lee-ye STA mee-lee-ART-taf roob-LYEY), with сто in its genitive ста. около 1,6 триллиона рублей is read около одной целой шести десятых триллиона рублей (O-ka-la ad-NOY TSE-loy shes-TEE dee-sya-TYKH tree-lee-O-na roob-LYEY), and the whole decimal phrase declines because около is in front of it. порядка 5 процентов ВВП is порядка пяти процентов ВВП (pa-RYAD-ka pee-TEE pra-TSEN-taf), with пять in the genitive пяти.

Fractions are the last piece and they are simpler than they look. половина (pa-la-VEE-na) and треть (TRYET) and четверть (CHYET-vert) are nouns, so they govern the genitive: половина бюджета, треть дохода, четверть опрошенных. Above one they take the ordinary counting forms: две трети бюджета (dvye TRYE-tee byoo-DZHE-ta, 'two thirds of the budget'), три четверти опрошенных (tree CHYET-ver-tee a-PRO-shen-nykh, 'three quarters of those surveyed'). полтора and полторы mean 'one and a half' and take the genitive singular: полтора часа, полторы недели, полтора миллиона рублей.
lessons.example:
Read four figures from a real report aloud, one at a time, and check each against its written form. 29 904 рубля: двадцать девять тысяч девятьсот четыре рубля (DVAT-tsat DYE-veet TY-seech dee-veet-SOT chee-TY-ree roob-LYA). 778,5 тысячи рублей: семьсот семьдесят восемь целых пять десятых тысячи рублей (seem-SOT SYEM-de-seet VO-seem TSE-lykh pyat dee-sya-TYKH TY-see-chee roob-LYEY), or in the shorter spoken version, семьсот семьдесят восемь с половиной тысяч рублей. 1,6 триллиона: одна целая шесть десятых триллиона (ad-NA TSE-la-ya shest dee-sya-TYKH tree-lee-O-na). 17 процентов: семнадцать процентов (seem-NAT-tsat pra-TSEN-taf).

Now put the same figures into sentences with governing words in front, and watch the case spread inward. Более 100 миллиардов рублей: более ста миллиардов рублей (BO-lee-ye STA mee-lee-ART-taf roob-LYEY). Около 1,6 триллиона рублей: около одной целой шести десятых триллиона рублей (O-ka-la ad-NOY TSE-loy shes-TEE dee-sya-TYKH tree-lee-O-na roob-LYEY). Порядка 5 процентов ВВП: порядка пяти процентов ВВП (pa-RYAD-ka pee-TEE pra-TSEN-taf vee-vee-PYE). In each one the first word after the preposition is the one that shows the case, and every numeral after it follows.

Finally a price sentence that moves in both directions. В октябре курс вырос с 80,68 до 84,43 рубля за доллар (v ak-teeb-RYE koors VY-ras s VO-seem-de-see-tee roob-LYEY shes-tee-de-SYA-tee va-see-MEE ka-PYE-yek da VO-seem-de-see-tee chee-ty-RYOKH roob-LYEY sa-ra-KA tree ka-PYE-yek za DO-lar, 'in October the rate rose from 80 rubles 68 kopecks to 84 rubles 43 kopecks per dollar'). Two decimal prices, both in the genitive because of с and до, and both read as rubles and kopecks rather than as comma numbers. This is the sentence to practise until it is smooth, because it contains every operation in the lesson at once.
lessons.question: You are reading a bulletin and the text says «инфляция составила 6,35 процента». How do you read the figure aloud, and why is it процента rather than процентов?
lessons.answer: «шесть целых тридцать пять сотых процента»: the decimal fraction governs the genitive singular, so the noun is процента even though the integer part is above four.
lessons.distractor: «шесть запятая тридцать пять процентов»: the number is above four, so the noun takes the genitive plural.
lessons.correction: A comma in a Russian figure is not the word запятая in a news reading; it separates the whole number from the fraction, and the fraction is named. 6,35 is шесть целых тридцать пять сотых, and the noun after a decimal fraction is genitive singular, which is процента. The distracter applies the five-and-above rule to the integer and reads the comma as the punctuation mark, and both moves are wrong in this register. The same logic gives 0,11 процента and 1,5 процента, while a whole number gives 6 процентов and 7 процентов. The test is whether there is a fraction at all, not how large the number is.

depth.definitions: A decimal fraction is a number written with a comma in Russian, read as whole units plus tenths or hundredths. Approximation is the expression of a figure as near rather than exact, marked by около, более, менее, до or порядка. A fraction word is a noun such as половина, треть or четверть, which governs the genitive of what it divides. Per cent government is the choice between процент, процента and процентов according to the numeral in front. The reading form of a figure is the spoken phrase, which restores the counted nouns that the written abbreviation leaves out.
depth.mechanism:
Read a figure in four passes. First, group it: thousands, millions, billions, trillions, each group read as a number and closed with its noun. Second, read each group's last word and let it choose the ending of the noun that follows: один рубль, два рубля, пять рублей. Third, look at the word in front of the whole phrase. If it is около, более, менее, порядка, с or до, put the first numeral into the genitive and let the rest of the phrase follow it into the same case. Fourth, if there is a comma, read the whole part with целых, the fraction with десятых or сотых, and put any following noun into the genitive singular.

Money adds one step. A written price with a decimal, such as 80,68 рубля, is read as rubles and kopecks: восемьдесят рублей шестьдесят восемь копеек. The written рубля is a grammatical agreement with the decimal; the spoken form counts the rubles with рублей and the kopecks with копеек, and neither word keeps the ending it had on the page.

For prices in a sentence, the verb decides the preposition. стоит and составляет take the bare accusative. вырос, снизился and упал take на plus the accusative for the amount and до plus the genitive for the endpoint. A range takes с plus the genitive and до plus the genitive. The numerals inside each phrase then follow the case of the phrase.
depth.secondExample:
Read a short bulletin paragraph and mark every figure before reading it aloud. Пенсия по старости к концу 2027 года составит 29 904 рубля (PYEN-see-ya pa sta-RA-stee k kant-SOO DVYE TY-see-chee DVAT-tsat seed-MO-va GO-da sas-TA-veet DVAT-tsat DYE-veet TY-seech dee-veet-SOT chee-TY-ree roob-LYA, 'the old-age pension will reach 29,904 roubles by the end of 2027'). Материнский капитал на первого ребёнка составит 778,5 тысячи рублей (ma-tee-REEN-skee ka-pee-TAL na PYER-va-va ree-BYON-ka sas-TA-veet seem-SOT SYEM-de-seet VO-seem TSE-lykh pyat dee-sya-TYKH TY-see-chee roob-LYEY, 'the maternity capital for a first child will be 778.5 thousand roubles'). The report prints 778,5 тысяч, which is common in newspapers; the normative form after a decimal is the genitive singular тысячи, and that is what a careful reader says.

Now the same paragraph with the figures in oblique positions, which is what a follow-up sentence does. На эти цели направят более 100 миллиардов рублей (na E-tee TSE-lee na-PRAF-lyat BO-lee-ye STA mee-lee-ART-taf roob-LYEY, 'more than 100 billion roubles will be allocated to these purposes'). Расходы вырастут примерно на 17 процентов (ras-KHO-dy VY-ras-toot pree-MYER-na na seem-NAT-tsat pra-TSEN-taf, 'spending will grow by about seventeen per cent'). The first sentence has более forcing the genitive on сто, the second has на forcing the accusative on семнадцать, and neither figure keeps the form it would have in a table.
depth.mistake:
The first error is reading a comma as the word запятая. In a news reading the comma names a fraction: целых and сотых or десятых, not запятая.

The second error is ignoring the governing preposition. A learner reads более 100 миллиардов as более сто миллиардов, leaving сто in the nominative because the number looks like a label. более requires the genitive, so сто becomes ста, and the same repair gives около пятисот, порядка пяти, менее десяти.

The third error is the per cent ending after a decimal, as in 6,35 процентов. The decimal governs the genitive singular, so it is процента. The repair is to ask whether there is a fraction, not how big the integer is.

A fourth error is the money phrase, where a learner reads 80,68 рубля as восемьдесят целых шестьдесят восемь сотых рубля. That is grammatical in a mathematical register and wrong in a bulletin, where the price is read as rubles and kopecks. The repair is to restore the two counted nouns: восемьдесят рублей шестьдесят восемь копеек.
depth.application:
Take five figures from a report you can read, write them out in words, and read them aloud. Include one integer above a thousand, one decimal percentage, one price with kopecks, one figure after более or около, and one fraction such as две трети. Check each against the four-pass method and mark which pass decided the ending.

Then write a six-sentence budget paragraph about your own work or household with at least four figures: a total, a monthly figure, a percentage change, and an approximate figure with около. Read it aloud at bulletin speed, then read it again slowly, stopping after each numeral to name its case.

Finish by reading the four figures from the example in one breath each, without looking at the words. If the phrases come out whole, the lesson has done its work; if you stumble at the second group, the thousands are still being read as separate numbers rather than as a phrase.
depth.summary: Read figures in groups, let the last numeral of each group choose the noun ending, and let any governing word in front put the whole phrase into its case. Decimals are read with целых and сотых or десятых, and they force the following noun into the genitive singular. Money with a decimal is read as rubles and kopecks, not as a fraction of a ruble. около, более, менее and порядка take the genitive, на takes the accusative for a change, and с and до take the genitive for a range.

readings.note: Read the sections headed Пенсии, зарплаты, выплаты and Об инфраструктуре. They contain the figures this lesson reads aloud: 29 904 рубля, 778,5 тысячи рублей (the report prints 778,5 тысяч, and the normative form after a decimal is тысячи), более 100 миллиардов рублей, 17 процентов and порядка 5 процентов. Read each figure in its sentence rather than in isolation, because the governing word is what decides the case. Caveat: this is a newspaper report, not a grammar, it reflects the budget as presented in October 2026, and the figures will age; use it for the register and the number shapes, not as current data.

readings.title: Rossiyskaya Gazeta, currency report, 30 October 2026
readings.note: Read the first four paragraphs, where the official rates are given as 80,68 рубля за доллар, 89,82 рубля за евро and 12,08 рубля за юань, with the month-earlier figures beside them. This is the best short text for price reading, because every figure is a decimal with kopecks and every one is followed by за plus a currency. Caveat: it is a news article with forecasts, the rates are those of 30 October 2026, and the analysis is one newspaper's selection of expert opinion rather than a neutral summary.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Expressing approximately'
readings.note: Read the whole page. It gives около plus the genitive, the inverted order часа два (cha-SA DVA, 'about two hours'), and the paired numerals два-три for 'two or three', and it notes that the inverted order is the conversational way rather than the bookish one. That is the approximation system this lesson uses in prices and figures. Caveat: the Cyrillic is in a legacy font and arrives garbled, and the page is short enough that the examples carry most of the information.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Numeral inversion means approximately'
readings.note: Read this two-line page for the rule in its shortest form: reversing the numeral and its noun means 'approximately', so двадцать стаканов is twenty glasses and стаканов двадцать is about twenty glasses. It is worth seeing the rule stated so baldly, because the inversion is easy to miss in a report where it signals that a figure is an estimate. Caveat: it is a single example and a single sentence, with no discussion of when the inversion is idiomatic.

readings.title: Wikipedia: Russian grammar, section 'Numerals'
readings.note: Read the short Numerals section. It states the two facts this lesson builds on: a noun stays in the nominative after один (один рубль), and after other numbers it is declined to the genitive (десять рублей), with a link to the full paradigms under Russian declension. Use it as a second opinion on the bands, not as a table. Caveat: the section is a summary of a few lines, it is crowd-edited, and it does not treat decimals, money or approximation at all, so the reading for those is Cornell's numbers page.

visual.title: Four-pass reading ladder for a figure
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: one large figure at the top, four horizontal passes below it, each pass narrowing the phrase until the spoken form is complete. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, write the figure at the top: 29 904 рубля. Under it draw the first pass and group the digits: 29 тысяч and 904. Label the groups 'thousands' and 'units', because the group boundary decides where тысяч goes.

Step 2, in the second pass write the last word of each group: девять and четыре. Beside each, write the noun form it chooses: тысяч after девять, рубля after четыре. This pass is the last-word rule from lesson 116.

Step 3, in the third pass add the governing word. Write более 29 904 рубля and change the first numeral to its genitive: более двадцати девяти тысяч... Mark the arrow that carries the case inward through the whole phrase.
Step 4, in the fourth pass write the spoken form in full: двадцать девять тысяч девятьсот четыре рубля, and beside it the same phrase under более. Compare the two and mark the words that changed.

Step 5, add a side box for decimals: 6,35 процента, read as шесть целых тридцать пять сотых процента, with the label 'fraction governs genitive singular'. Draw a line from the comma to the noun to show that the fraction, not the integer, is in charge.

per cent (genitive singular after a decimal)
per cent (genitive plural after 5 and above)
of the order of, around (with the genitive)

questions.prompt: You are writing 'about twenty-two textbooks' in a report. Which phrase is correct?
questions.correction: около governs the genitive, so every word inside the phrase declines: двадцати двух учебников (dvat-tsa-TEE dvookh oo-CHEB-nee-kaf). The noun is genitive plural because an oblique numeral cancels the genitive singular rule that applies in the nominative. The distracter leaves the numeral and the noun in their nominative shapes, which is the commonest import from English, where a preposition does not change the number words.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'the trip took two days and nights'?
questions.correction: сутки has no singular, so the two-to-four band cannot produce a genitive singular from it and the collective двое takes over: двое суток (DVO-ye SOO-tak). The distracter applies the ordinary два to a plural-only noun, which produces a phrase that is understood and not said. Compare два часа, two hours, where the noun has a singular and the ordinary numeral is correct.

questions.prompt: A notice must say that the meeting takes place on the third of March. Which sentence is correct?
questions.correction: A date that locates an event is a genitive phrase with no preposition: третьего марта (TRYET-ye-va MAR-ta). в is used with months in the prepositional (в марте) and with clock times in the accusative (в три часа), not with a calendar date. The distracter transfers the time preposition в to a construction that does not take it, which is the central confusion of lesson 118.

questions.prompt: The timetable says the train leaves at 8:07. Which is the traditional reading of that time?
questions.correction: The traditional clock counts the minutes of the hour that is coming, so 8:07 is seven minutes of the ninth hour: в семь минут девятого (f syem mee-NOOT dee-VYA-ta-va). восьмого would make it 7:07, an hour earlier, which is the same off-by-one that produces половина пятого for 5:30. The minutes are nominative plural and the hour is genitive, and only the ordinal changes with the hour.

questions.prompt: You are reading a bulletin that says «инфляция составила 6,35 процента». How do you read the figure aloud?
questions.answer: шесть целых тридцать пять сотых процента
questions.correction: A comma in a Russian figure separates the whole part from the fraction, and the fraction is named: шесть целых тридцать пять сотых (shest TSE-lykh TREET-tsat pyat SO-tykh). The noun after a decimal is genitive singular, so процента, even though the integer is above four. The distracter reads the comma as the punctuation mark запятая and applies the five-and-above rule, and both moves belong to a different register.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that it means 'here is the colleague I spoke to yesterday': «Вот коллега, ___ я говорил вчера».
questions.correction: говорить о ком, 'to speak about someone', takes о plus the prepositional, so the relative word is котором and the preposition stands in front: о котором (a ka-TO-ram). The distracter chooses the genitive/accusative form because it sounds like the object of говорил, but говорил does not take a direct object here. The preposition is the signal: if you can hear the preposition, you can hear the case.

questions.prompt: A colleague reports a fact: 'he said the project is ready'. Which sentence is correct?
questions.correction: сказать in the reporting sense takes что, and the clause keeps the tense of the original statement: Он сказал, что проект готов (on ska-ZAL, SHTO pra-YEKT ga-TOF). чтобы would turn the report into an instruction, which requires a past-tense verb and means 'he said the project should be ready'. The distracter marks a fact as a wish, which is the error lesson 112 diagnoses.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'I want you to come earlier'?
questions.answer: Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл раньше.
questions.distractor: Я хочу, что ты пришёл раньше.
questions.correction: Two subjects, I want and you come, so the construction is чтобы plus the past form: Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл раньше (ya kha-CHOO, SHTO-by ty pree-SHYOL RAN-she). The past form refers to a future arrival, because чтобы has no tense of its own. The distracter is the literal translation of 'I want that you came', which is the commonest mistake with this pair.

questions.prompt: Complete the unreal condition: «Если бы у нас было время, мы ___ всё».
questions.correction: An unreal condition puts бы in both clauses and a past form in both: Если бы у нас было время, мы бы проверили всё (YEs-lee by oo nas BY-la VRYE-mya, my by pra-VYE-ree-lee VSYO). The future проверим belongs to the real conditional, where the world is still open. The distracter keeps the second half real while the first half is unreal, which is the incoherence lesson 113 warns about.

questions.prompt: Complete the real condition: «Если ты позвонишь, я ___».
questions.correction: A real condition takes ordinary indicative verbs, so the main clause is a future: Если ты позвонишь, я отвечу (YEs-lee ty paz-va-NEESH, ya at-VYE-choo). The perfective future in the если-clause names a single completed call, and the main clause names the consequence. The distracter imports бы from the unreal pattern and turns a plan into a hypothesis.

questions.prompt: Complete the concessive sentence: «___ дождь, мы пошли гулять».
questions.correction: The obstacle here is a noun, so the pattern is несмотря на plus the accusative: Несмотря на дождь, мы пошли гулять (nee-smat-RYA na dosht). несмотря на то что needs a clause with a subject and a verb, as in несмотря на то что шёл дождь. The distracter attaches the clause introducer to a noun phrase, which is the mixed construction lesson 114 diagnoses.

questions.prompt: Which is the spoken-register equivalent of «студент, читающий книгу»?
questions.correction: A present active participle becomes который plus a present-tense finite verb: читающий book becomes который читает (ka-TO-ryy chee-TA-yet). The distracter keeps the participle ending after который, which is double marking; once the relative word is there, the verb is finite. Cornell's equation is the rule behind the conversion: written participles equal spoken который clauses.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is correct for 'five books'?
questions.correction: Five and above take the genitive plural, so the noun is книг: пять книг (pyat kneek). The distracter uses the genitive singular, which belongs to the two-to-four band (две книги), and it is the error that comes from applying one numeral rule to all numbers above one. The same ladder gives пять столов and пять окон.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: «Мне двадцать два ___».
questions.correction: The last word of the numeral is два, so the noun is in the genitive singular: двадцать два года (DVAT-tsat dva GO-da). лет belongs to the five-and-above band, as in двадцать пять лет. The distracter applies the band of the first word rather than the last, which is the error the backwards reading habit is designed to prevent.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that it means 'we met on the second of February': «Мы встретились ___».
questions.correction: Locating an event on a date takes the genitive: второго февраля (fta-RO-va feev-ra-LYA). The nominative второе февраля names the date, as in Сегодня второе февраля. The distracter confuses naming with locating, and the month stays genitive in both, which is why the error is easy to miss.

questions.prompt: Which preposition completes «Я прочитал книгу ___ два часа» so that it means 'I read the book in two hours'?
questions.correction: A perfective verb with за plus the accusative measures the time it took to finish: Я прочитал книгу за два часа (ya pra-chee-TAL KNEE-goo za dva cha-SA). через means 'after' and points forward from now, as in через два часа, 'in two hours'. The distracter is a time preposition in the right case and the wrong meaning, which is why the aspect of the verb has to be checked before the preposition is chosen.

questions.prompt: How do you read «более 100 миллиардов рублей» aloud?
questions.correction: более governs the genitive, so сто becomes ста and the phrase is more than a hundred billion: более ста миллиардов рублей (BO-lee-ye STA mee-lee-ART-taf roob-LYEY). The distracter leaves the numeral in its dictionary form because it looks like a label on a chart. The same repair gives около пятисот and порядка пяти, and it is the reason figures in a report have to be read as phrases rather than as digits.
